d6666e.title: IDOR vulnerability in appointments DELETE endpoint
d6666e.content:
The DELETE /api/appointments/:id endpoint in app/api/appointments/route.ts lacks authorization checks to verify that the authenticated user owns the appointment being deleted. Only an Authorization header is required, with no validation of ownership or access control based on the authenticated user's identity. This enables Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) where any authenticated user can delete any other user's appointment by ID.

Technical details:
- File: /workspace/front/app/api/appointments/route.ts
- Method: DELETE
- Vulnerability: IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference)
- Impact: Unauthorized deletion of appointments belonging to other users
- Root cause: Missing ownership verification in DELETE handler

Steps to reproduce:
1. Authenticate as User A
2. Note the ID of User B's appointment (can be discovered via GET /api/appointments)
3. Send DELETE request to /api/appointments/{id} with User A's authorization header
4. Appointment is deleted without ownership validation

This is a critical authorization bypass that allows appointment deletion across user boundaries.
